title: LIVE WATER QUALITY
freshness_label: SOURCE CHECKED HOURLY / LATEST VALID OBSERVATION
source_name: USGS Water Quality Portal (WQX E. coli / enterococci / fecal coliform) + EPA BEACON beach-advisory framework + EPA 2012 RWQC & 1976 Red Book thresholds
variable: Swim-water bacteria (E. coli, enterococci, fecal coliform — CFU per 100 mL) normalized to one human-health concern index; official advisories/closures take display priority
source_units: CFU per 100 mL (colony-forming units per 100 mL)
display_units: E. coli-equivalent CFU/100 mL (log scale) -> 13-step human-health gradient
temporal: Sources checked hourly. Monitoring agencies publish new samples only when sampling occurs (typically weekly in swim season, rarely in winter). New observation -> used. No new observation -> latest valid observation retained up to 7 days, then treated as stale/no-data. SOURCE CHECKED HOURLY is distinct from SOURCE DATA PUBLICATION FREQUENCY.
what: Available authoritative evidence of fecal-indicator bacterial contamination relevant to human recreational use of Great Lakes waters, consolidated into one human-health gradient. E. coli and enterococci are indicator organisms for fecal contamination and potential pathogen risk - they are not themselves identified as disease-causing pathogens in every sample, and this layer does not detect every pathogen.
coverage_note: Visual scope spans 100% of the five Great Lakes water surfaces (shared NOAA shoreline mask). Where no defensible observation exists, water stays transparent as NO DATA (slate swatch in key) - never as zero/low bacteria.
